premise: A rainy Sunday at the flower shop, and the till won't open.

lines.speaker: chr_seedHana
lines.text:
Rainy Sundays are supposed to be slow and cozy, not the day my till decides to lock up like a stubborn tulip bud!

Dad, if I jiggle this lever while you hit the drawer, will that help, or am I about to lose a fingernail?

lines.speaker: chr_seedTakeshi
lines.text:
Step back from that lever, Hana. That drawer's like a frozen switch on a cold morning — force it and you'll snap something you can't fix with duct tape.  

Rin, hand me that flathead screwdriver from under the counter and nobody loses a fingernail today.

lines.speaker: chr_seedRin
lines.text: found it. also watching you two try to beat a cash register is the best content this shop's had all week.

lines.speaker: chr_seedHana
lines.text:
I just wanted to buy my own croissant, is that so much to ask on a rainy day?

Rin, keep filming and I'm putting you on watering duty for the ferns. All of them. Kai, you're the tech person here — any brilliant ideas before Dad performs surgery?

lines.speaker: chr_seedTakeshi
lines.text:
Printer's probably the culprit — the receipt feed jams and the till sulks. Check the little display for an error code first, Kai.

Some days you're the train, some days you're the cow on the tracks. This drawer's the cow.

lines.speaker: chr_seedRin
lines.text:
ferns are your job, i'm just the audience. dad's right though, check the display first.

and kai, if you fix this you're officially more useful than my entire studio's it guy. low bar, but still.

lines.speaker: chr_seedHana
lines.text:
No pressure, Kai, but my whole morning hangs on you now!

Honestly the bouquet orders can wait, it's the croissants at the station bakery I'm worried about — they sell out by ten.

lines.speaker: chr_seedTakeshi
lines.text:
Croissant deadline, now that's a real emergency. Thirty years on the rails, I never once left the platform late. Bakeries are no different.

That screwdriver's getting warm in my hand, Kai. You've got until the coffee goes cold — and the coffee's already coffee.

lines.speaker: chr_seedRin
lines.text: it's 9:40, so if kai doesn't crack it in twenty i'm calling the bakery and pretending to be you, hana. sacrifices must be made.

lines.speaker: chr_seedHana
lines.text:
You wouldn't survive one conversation with Mrs. Okada, she asks about everyone's love life and you don't even have one!

Fine. Plan B is I slip a note under the bakery door asking them to save me two, and we accept being known as the flaky croissant people forever.

lines.speaker: chr_seedTakeshi
lines.text:
I raised two daughters. I can outwait a bakery, a till, and the both of you combined.

Now quit chatting. The screwdriver's older than Rin, so it's earned the right to do nothing until we've read that error code.

lines.speaker: chr_seedRin
lines.text:
mrs. okada can ask me whatever she wants, i'll just lie creatively. you're welcome.

kai, seriously though. what's the screen say.

lines.speaker: chr_seedHana
lines.text:
Kai, I'm holding my breath here — say it's something dumb like a paper jam and I'll kiss you in front of my whole family.

Which I'll do anyway, but the paper jam sweetens it!

lines.speaker: chr_seedTakeshi
lines.text:
Focus, Kai. A screen's like a signal box — read it before you pull anything.

If it's a jam, you owe me a croissant too. And Hana, no kissing till the drawer's open. Shop rules.

lines.speaker: chr_seedRin
lines.text:
shop rules are fake, dad made them up thirty seconds ago.

but yeah, error code, kai. we're all invested now. this is basically a raid boss and you're the only one with a key.

lines.speaker: chr_seedHana
lines.text:
Raid boss is right, it's wearing us all down! I've been standing here so long my apron's got a crease in it.

Dad, shop rules can't be made up on rainy days, that's practically constitutional law.

lines.speaker: chr_seedTakeshi
lines.text:
Rainy days are exactly when rules get made. Nobody's coming to stop me.

Enough stalling. Kai, read it out loud — I'll tell you if it's a jam or a jam with extra paperwork.

lines.speaker: chr_seedRin
lines.text:
y'all have turned one error code into a family drama. it's honestly impressive.

kai, i'd bail you out but my specialty is game balance, not cash drawers. you're on your own, hero.

lines.speaker: chr_seedTakeshi
lines.text:
Hero business runs on coffee and patience. Good thing we've got one of those.

Kai. Screen. Out loud. That croissant's not going to save itself.

lines.speaker: chr_seedHana
lines.text:
Rin, the least you could do is pretend to google it dramatically instead of narrating our suffering!

Kai, whatever the code says, I believe in you. If it's gibberish, that's still more than the rest of us have managed.

lines.speaker: chr_seedTakeshi
lines.text:
Google won't fix a drawer, it'll just tell you twelve ways to be wrong. This is a lever and a spring. Simple as a train coupling.

Ten minutes, Kai, or I'm prying it myself and the bakery story becomes my obituary.

lines.speaker: chr_seedRin
lines.text:
"twelve ways to be wrong" is just the google experience, dad's not wrong.

fine, grabbing my phone. kai, if you look at the screen and it says something like e-04 i'm gonna laugh so hard.

lines.speaker: chr_seedHana
lines.text:
Stop threatening my shop with dramatic obituaries, you're not allowed to die in here, I just mopped!

Dad's got a point though, Kai — it really is just a lever and a spring under all the beeping.

lines.speaker: chr_seedTakeshi
lines.text:
Nine forty-five. Coffee's cold, so it's clock time now.

Kai, push the release latch under the drawer and give it one clean pull. Like uncoupling a car — firm, not angry.

lines.speaker: chr_seedRin
lines.text:
"firm, not angry" is how i wish my raid team took feedback.

do it, kai. i'll count to three and if it doesn't open i'm blaming you forever. one. two.

lines.speaker: chr_seedTakeshi
lines.text:
Don't count at a mechanic. Count at your raid team.

One clean pull, Kai. On my mark.

lines.speaker: chr_seedHana
lines.text:
I can't watch, I'm staring at the peonies instead. They look how I feel. Under a lot of pressure, slightly droopy!

If this works I'm declaring croissants on the house for everyone. Forever. Including Mrs. Okada.

lines.speaker: chr_seedRin
lines.text:
three.

that was anticlimactic. i want my money back.

lines.speaker: chr_seedTakeshi
lines.text:
Ha. There she blows. Like the six-forty express, right on schedule.

Somebody check the receipt roll so it doesn't jam again next Sunday, and Hana, those croissants better be warm.

lines.speaker: chr_seedHana
lines.text:
It opened! Kai, you beautiful nerd, I could actually cry over a cash drawer and I'm not even embarrassed!

Warm croissants, all four of us, my treat. Rain's easing too — see, the day's unfolding like a tulip after all.

lines.speaker: chr_seedRin
lines.text:
kai gets the win, fine. i'll take the free croissant as my reward for moral support.

rain's easing, so now dad can tell us the cow-on-the-tracks story on the walk over. again. fourth time this month.
